harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Enabled XFS user-quota accounting on node1's root filesystem (rootflags=uquota via grubby + fstab usrquota, requiring one reboot to activate), created the datauser account, set its /srv/data home directory, applied a filesystem-enforced 100MB (soft=hard) XFS user quota for datauser, and verified enforcement both before and after the mandatory node restart-evidence reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: AlmaLinux 9.6, single XFS root filesystem mounted noquota, no /srv/data or datauser yet
Added rootflags=uquota to all kernel entries via grubby, and usrquota to the root entry in /etc/fstab
Captured pre-activation boot_id and rebooted node1 to activate the XFS uquota mount option (functionally required, not the evidence reboot)
Verified / now mounted with usrquota after reboot
Created datauser (nologin, home=/srv/data), created /srv/data owned by datauser:datauser mode 700
Set XFS quota: xfs_quota limit bsoft=100m bhard=100m datauser on /
Verified quota report shows datauser limited to 100M
Tested enforcement: dd write of 90MB succeeded, further dd write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' at ~99MB actual usage
Cleaned up test files, wrote a persistent marker file into /srv/data with sha256 for later verification
Captured pre-restart boot_id (mandatory protocol baseline)
Restarted node1 via 'reboot', polled until exec was available again
Confirmed boot_id changed (proof of actual restart, not just reconnect)

Verified post-restart: / still mounted usrquota, xfs quota still 100M for datauser, marker.txt content and sha256 unchanged, and a fresh dd write again failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' confirming enforcement survived the restart
Cleaned up post-reboot test file, left only the marker file in /srv/data

evidence.requirement: Pre-change baseline: filesystem type, mount options, no existing datauser/quota
evidence.summary: Shows root is XFS mounted 'noquota', datauser does not yet exist, /srv/data does not yet exist

evidence.requirement: XFS uquota accounting enabled on the filesystem hosting /srv/data
evidence.summary: grubby adds rootflags=uquota, fstab updated with usrquota, and post-activation-reboot mount output shows '/dev/vda4 on / type xfs (...,usrquota)'

evidence.requirement: datauser account and /srv/data directory created and owned correctly
evidence.summary: useradd datauser (nologin, home /srv/data) and /srv/data created with owner datauser:datauser mode 700

evidence.requirement: 100MB quota limit configured for datauser, filesystem-enforced
evidence.summary: xfs_quota limit set bsoft=100m bhard=100m for datauser; report confirms 100M/100M limits

evidence.requirement: Quota enforcement demonstrated (writes beyond 100MB rejected by the filesystem)
evidence.summary: 90MB write succeeds; subsequent write fails mid-stream with 'dd: error writing: Disk quota exceeded' at ~99MB usage, proving kernel-level XFS enforcement

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline (boot id + service/data health) before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 368441cc-d525-4a81-95cd-a216a963a2c9, and wrote/verified marker.txt (sha256 0822dc01...) in /srv/data as data health proof

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: restart acknowledgement and connectivity loss/recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent exec calls show connection reset/timeout confirming the node actually went down

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: proof of changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 4b91a1cc-ef2b-4305-bc7a-a8e04a7d81a3, different from the pre-restart value 368441cc-..., proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: post-restart recovery of required services/data and continued quota enforcement
evidence.summary: After restart, / still mounted usrquota, datauser quota still 100M, marker.txt content/sha256 unchanged, and a new dd write again fails with 'Disk quota exceeded' at ~99MB, confirming enforcement persisted across reboot; test file cleaned up afterward

attempts.summary: Enabled XFS user-quota accounting on node1's root filesystem (rootflags=uquota via grubby + fstab usrquota, requiring one reboot to activate), created the datauser account, set its /srv/data home directory, applied a filesystem-enforced 100MB (soft=hard) XFS user quota for datauser, and verified enforcement both before and after the mandatory node restart-evidence reboot.
